newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel considers refurbishing Jerusalem holy site.
newsitem.headline: Israel considers refurbishing Jerusalem holy site.

text.p: Israel is considering refurbishing a Jewish holy site near Moslem shrines in Jerusalem's Old City, a spokesman for the Religious Affairs Ministry said on Tuesday.
The move was likely to irk Palestinians, who waged gun battles with Israeli troops last September after the Jewish state opened a second entrance to an archaeological tunnel in the Old City.

Religious Affairs Ministry spokesman Shimon Malka said officials decided in February to look into refurbishing an area in the Old City's Moslem quarter to give Jewish worshippers better access to another part of the Western Wall -- Judaism's holiest site -- known as the "Little Wall".
Jews from all over the world worship at the Western Wall, a retaining wall which supported the biblical Jewish Temple.
"The two deputy ministers for religious affairs visited the Little Wall two months ago and stated then that their intention was to refurbish it and open it to prayers for Jews," Malka told Reuters.
He said the plan was under consideration and security issues would also be taken into account.
The Western Wall's close proximity to al-Aqsa mosque, Islam's third holiest shrine, has made the site particularly sensitive in a city holy to Jews, Moslems and Christians.

"We don't recognise any place except the Western Wall in the southwest corner of the mosque as holy to Jews. It is nonsense to say that any other area is a holy site," said Hasan Tahboob, a member of the Palestinian Authority in charge of religious affairs.
Fifteen Israelis and 61 Palestinians died last September in the tunnel-related violence.

A Hebron accord between Israel and the PLO four months later put peace moves back on course but Israel's groundbreaking for a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March again plunged peace moves into crisis.

Israel captured East Jerusalem, including the Old City, in the 1967 Middle East war and later annexed it as its indivisible capital. The PLO claims East Jerusalem as the capital of a future Palestinian state.
